context.title: Christ Is Risen
context.summary: Paul restates the gospel of Christ's death and resurrection, lists the witnesses, and argues that because Christ rose, believers will be raised with new, imperishable bodies.
context.background: Some in Corinth said there is no resurrection of the dead (v. 12); many Greeks thought the body unimportant and bodily resurrection absurd (Acts 17:32). Verses 3–7 are a summary Paul says he 'received', which many scholars consider among the earliest Christian statements of faith. Paul notes that most of the five hundred witnesses were still alive (v. 6).

customs.note: Paul mentions this practice in passing to make an argument. What it was is unknown, and many explanations have been proposed.
The first sheaf of harvest was offered to God as a promise of the full harvest. Christ's resurrection guarantees the rest.

watchFor: 'If Christ be not raised' and its consequences (vv. 14–19).
The seed analogy for the resurrection body (vv. 36–44).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

people.name: Adam
people.summary: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Gen. 1:27-ch. 5).

places.name: Ephesus
places.summary: The capital of proconsular Asia, which was the western part of Asia Minor. It was colonized principally from Athens. In the time of the Romans it bore the title of “the first and greatest metropolis of Asia.”
